title: Signal · Sunday 1 November
overview: UBS beats on profit as its capital fight with Bern hardens, the Federal Council sets a timetable for binding AI rules, banks put AI agents to work, the AI labs raise big numbers and hard questions, and a record Binance theft meets AI-run attacks.

top.headline: UBS beats on profit as its capital fight with Bern hardens
top.summary: UBS reported third-quarter net profit of USD 2.7 billion on 28 October, with profit before tax up 27 percent to USD 3.6 billion and USD 55 billion of net new assets in Global Wealth Management. It now expects integration savings of about USD 13.7 billion by the end of 2026. Staff numbered just under 98,000 at the end of September, against more than 120,000 at UBS and Credit Suisse at the end of 2022, according to SRF.
top.background: On the results call, chief executive Sergio Ermotti called the Council of States' September vote very concerning, according to finews. It would make UBS back its foreign units with 90 percent CET1 capital, against the Federal Council's proposed full backing.
top.why: The outcome will set what UBS can return or invest for years. A finance ministry review reported by Reuters found a move to the US or Britain could prove as costly as the Swiss plans.
top.watch_next: A National Council committee began its review this week, with a vote possible in December.

top.headline: Federal Council sets Switzerland's path to binding AI rules
top.summary: On 28 October the Federal Council took note of progress in applying the Council of Europe AI Convention. OFCOM published a report on sector-specific measures and a Guide on an AI Code of Conduct, with suggested texts on 10 topics at three levels of detail. The consultation on binding rules is scheduled to begin in spring 2027.
top.background: The Federal Council decided on 12 February 2025 to ratify the convention. The planned rules are intended to cover transparency, data protection, non-discrimination, supervision and risk assessment; the guide is a voluntary toolkit for associations and businesses.
top.why: Swiss banks and insurers now have a timetable and a template. Firms can adopt the guide's texts now, alongside FINMA's existing guidance on AI governance, and test their controls before the draft arrives.
top.watch_next: Whether the spring draft relies on sector supervisors such as FINMA or sets duties across the economy.

top.headline: Banks move AI agents into daily work as supervisors count wide adoption
top.summary: Pedro Machado of the ECB's Supervisory Board said in an interview published on 30 October that around 85 percent of banks already use generative AI, from fraud detection and KYC documentation to transaction monitoring and credit scoring. ING said agentic AI cut approval times for complex Dutch mortgages from seven days to five. Deutsche Bank's private bank drafts source-of-wealth assessments with agentic AI that staff validate and approve, according to WealthBriefing.
top.background: Piguet Galland reported efficiency gains of around 10 percent from Microsoft Copilot, and Schwab switched on Claude for advisers on its platform. In an IFZ study reported by finews, 65 percent of Swiss and Liechtenstein banks expect to keep their core banking provider in ten years. Canada's largest banks now block third-party personal AI agents from online banking.
top.why: The work for banks has moved to control: sign-off, testing and a reliable way to stop an agent. Machado also warned that frontier models shorten the time between a flaw being found and exploited.

top.headline: Anthropic files to list as OpenAI trims its round and spending jitters spread
top.summary: Anthropic published its listing prospectus this week, with revenue above USD 16 billion in the first half of 2026, according to SRF. OpenAI has lowered its funding target to USD 20 billion, with USD 11 billion secured so far, according to the Financial Times and the Wall Street Journal as reported by TechCrunch. Alphabet fell 12 percent on 29 October, its worst day on record.
top.background: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft have outlined more than USD 740 billion of capital spending this year, and investors are now focused on free cash flow and debt, TechCrunch reported. Releases continued: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra at USD 1 per million input tokens, Google's Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber defenders first, and open weights for Mistral Large 4.
top.why: Capable models keep getting cheaper while funding the labs gets harder. For banks buying AI, that argues for contracts that keep the option to switch providers.

top.headline: Record USD 6.36 billion Binance theft and AI-run attacks test security
top.summary: An attacker moved about USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains on 29 October, most of it within about 20 minutes, according to TRM Labs, which attributes the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor unit. It is the largest crypto theft on record. On 31 October SRF reported that Binance had replaced 90 percent of the stolen assets; the attackers got in through an employee's hacked laptop.
top.background: CrowdStrike said a China-based group used the AI-driven ARTEX framework, with DeepSeek and a second commercial model, against more than 200 organisations from 17 October. Wiz counted at least nine AI developer platforms that disclosed incidents in October.
top.why: One compromised laptop moved billions in minutes, and attackers now run AI agents at scale. Banks building digital asset custody, or wiring agents into their systems, face the same access-control questions.

items.headline: CIBC chooses Thought Machine's Vault Core for its retail banking overhaul
items.summary: CIBC is turning to Thought Machine for a multi-year overhaul of its retail banking technology, beginning with its digital bank Simplii Financial, where an account built in less than a year is already in pilot, according to Fintech News Switzerland. CIBC co-led Thought Machine's Series E earlier this year with a GBP 30 million investment.
items.why: A large bank phasing in a cloud-native core gives Swiss banks, most of which expect to keep their vendor for a decade, a reference for gradual migration.

items.headline: Goldman Sachs joins EquiLend's 1Source ledger for securities finance
items.summary: Goldman Sachs now uses 1Source, EquiLend's distributed ledger for securities lending and financing, according to EquiLend's release. BNY and National Bank of Canada already send live transactions to it, and EquiLend says it reduces breaks and removes reconciliations.
items.why: Shared ledgers for post-trade data are reaching production at major dealers, which matters to custodians and securities finance desks in Zurich and Geneva.

items.headline: Julius Baer starts a CHF 600 million buyback after FINMA closes its case
items.summary: Julius Baer will start a share buyback of up to CHF 600 million on 2 November on a second trading line, to be completed within a year, according to finews. FINMA's conclusion at the end of September of proceedings over private debt deals with René Benko and Russian PEP clients allowed the bank to apply.
items.why: Shows the bank has room to return capital again now that the enforcement case is closed.

items.headline: Researchers show a shared ChatGPT link could take over accounts; OpenAI closed the hole
items.summary: Parameter Labs found an exploit against ChatGPT's sandboxed HTML previews that let a shared link reach a signed-in user's private data, Simon Willison wrote on 31 October. OpenAI closed the hole and paid a USD 5,000 bug bounty.
items.why: Sharing and preview features in AI assistants are an attack surface; banks rolling out chat assistants should review how links and previews are handled.

items.headline: AI chatbots get Swiss health insurance premiums mostly wrong in a test
items.summary: The Zone Media asked ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity 156 questions each about Swiss health insurance, according to Netzwoche. Of the 258 answers that gave an amount, 33 were correct.
items.why: General chatbots still produce confident wrong figures, so client-facing tools at insurers and banks need grounded data and checks before answers reach clients.

say_it_today: Around 85 percent of banks already use generative AI, the ECB's Pedro Machado said this week; the harder work now is sign-off, testing and a reliable way to stop an agent.
thread: AI became an operating matter for banks this week. A supervisor puts generative AI use at around 85 percent of banks, ING and Deutsche Bank describe agents in mortgage and KYC work, and Swiss private banks report measured gains. The rules are following the practice: Bern has a timetable for binding AI rules, and UK regulators say a business answers for what its AI agents do. Attackers use the same tools, as the Binance theft and CrowdStrike's ARTEX findings show. The common thread is control: who approved what, how agents are tested, and how fast they can be stopped.
